messages:
simon: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide probe/arbiter responsibilities for canary switchover. Main question: should the observer hold transient probe state (last-success, token, lease) or should the central arbiter keep the canonical lease and only consume metrics? Trying to avoid split-brain and accidental double-promote. :thinking:

jen: I lean central-lease. Observer can emit events/metrics but not be the source of truth. If observers temporarily lose connectivity we shouldn't trust their local view to flip traffic. Central arbiter manages leases with short TTLs and explicit renewals.

mike: Agree with central-lease for safety, but concerns: central becomes a perf hotspot and we add latency for every probe decision. Can we make it hybrid: local quick-failover (best-effort) then central confirmation for full promotion?

sasha: Hybrid sounds reasonable. Suggestion: two-phase promote: 1) observer can trigger a provisional state ("soft-divert") with graceful degradation, 2) arbiter performs reconciliation and issues a definitive promote after verifying signals. Provisional must be idempotent and scoped (tenant-level, small pct).

simon: +1. We should define the lease token semantics clearly. Proposal sketch:
```
# arbiter policy example
lease_ttl: 20s         # how long a promotion lease lasts without heartbeat
provisional_window: 10s # observer-only window for soft-divert
max_provisional_pct: 2  # max traffic % for provisional promotes
reconcile_timeout: 5s   # how long arbiter waits to collect metrics before final decision
```

jen: Important: observers must attach a signed promotion token to provisional actions so arbiter can validate origin and replay-safety. Token format: `ver:1|observer_id|nonce|sig` and we keep seen-nonces for TTL to avoid replay.

mike: Implementation note: storing seen-nonces globally could be heavy. Use a sharded bloom + TTL per-shard for approximate replay protection (accept small false positives). For strict safety customers can opt-in to exact nonce storage.

sasha: Also need metric fidelity contract: what counts as "success"? p50/p95, error-rate threshold, and sample size. Arbiter should reject promotes that don't meet sample-size. Example rule: error_rate < 0.5% AND p95_latency < 300ms AND samples >= 1000 in reconcile window.

simon: Ops concerns: how do we failback if arbiter is partitioned? We should prefer safe-degrade: if arbiter unreachable, observers revert provisional promotes after provisional_window expiry. No observer should attempt definitive promote when arbiter unreachable.

jen: That matches our SLA model. Also add explicit audit events for every provisional->final transition so Console & billing can reconcile.

mike: Small UX: add a `--force-finalize` operator endpoint guarded by RBAC for emergency ops (bypasses some heuristics but logs heavily).

deploy-bot: deploy status: canary-controller v2.3 deployed to staging at 1746123470 :rocket:

jen: Concrete next steps: I'll draft a short RFC appendix with token format, provisional flow diagram, and metric contract. Simon can take the arbiter interface shape and Mike will prototype bloom-based nonce store. Sasha will add sample-size checks to the observer telemetry shim.

simon: Thanks — I'll spin up a quick sequence diagram and put in the arch repo. If anyone has objections to the provisional-window approach, speak now. Otherwise I'll include as the default safe path. :thumbsup:
